cpic_recommendation: Initiate with a dose of 40 mg/day and if no clinical response and in the absence of adverse events after 2 weeks increase dose to 80 mg/day. If response is inadequate after 2 weeks, consider obtaining a plasma concentration 2 to 4 hours after dosing. If concentration is <200 ng/mL, consider a proportional dose increase to achieve a concentration to approach 400 ng/mL. If unacceptable side effects are present at any time, consider a reduction in dose.
source: FDA STRATTERA label section 2.5 (strong CYP2D6 inhibitor handled like a poor metabolizer); CPIC atomoxetine 2019 poor-metabolizer text
label_recommendation: FDA STRATTERA label, section 2.5 (adult, concomitant strong CYP2D6 inhibitor): "a longer titration interval of 4 weeks is recommended", "if ADHD symptoms fail to improve and the initial STRATTERA dosage is well tolerated". Starting, target and maximum dosages are the same as the label's standard adult table (40 mg/day start, 80 mg/day target, 100 mg/day maximum).
cpic_role: Supporting genotype-based context only (CPIC 2019 poor-metabolizer guidance); not an equally applicable dosing instruction for inhibitor-induced phenoconversion.
discrepancy_flag: Different guidance contexts: FDA labeling directly addresses strong CYP2D6 inhibitor coadministration and recommends a 4-week titration interval. CPIC 2019 provides genotype-based poor-metabolizer guidance with a 2-week response assessment. These recommendations should not be treated as interchangeable.

cpic_recommendation: Initiate with a dose of 40 mg/day and increase to 80 mg/day after 3 days. If no clinical response and in the absence of adverse events after 2 weeks, consider increasing dose to 100 mg/day. If no clinical response observed after 2 weeks, consider obtaining a peak plasma concentration (1 to 2 hours after dose administered). If <200 ng/mL, consider a proportional increase in dose to approach 400 ng/mL. Dosages greater than 100 mg/day may be needed to achieve target concentrations.
